reasoning_traces.think:
The core operators define a hierarchical fair-value inference system where composite power ratings (6-source mean) form a foundational kernel, while objective win% adjustments refine estimates through market-implied tiers. The MLB standings model introduces a logistic scaling path, enabling late-week updates without recalibration. Descriptive features like explosive play rates and PROE are excluded from fair-value blending due to lack of calibrated win-probability mappings. This ensures that only statistically robust, calibrated inputs contribute to the independent fair value. Failure modes include overfitting when source correlations exceed 0.9, and saturation in win% differentials. Dualities arise in how different sports' data are projected onto a common latent strength space, with the Skellam/Poisson path providing an alternative for event-level inference.
